findings.description: All printed answers on page 17 agree with independent readings or straight-segment interpolation of the displayed graphs. This is an inventory and numerical check, not acceptance.

The whole attached context page 16 was inspected. Its teaching supports estimating values between plotted points using connecting straight segments. Page 17 solutions use that method. Page 16 is context only and is not included as target-page entries.

Page 16 supplies temperatures 10, 15, 20, 23 and 18°C at 9 am, 10 am, 11 am, 12 pm and 1 pm. Straight-segment interpolation at 12:30 pm gives 20.5°C, whereas the printed worked answer is 20°C and the dashed guide is drawn at approximately 20°C. The question says estimate but gives no rounding precision. Preserve the source evidence and review the discrepancy; do not silently replace either value.

Page 16 says line graphs “always use continuous numerical data” and its third Key idea repeats this restriction. Page 17 includes gorilla counts over time, which are discrete counts. This teaching assertion needs bundled editorial review; it does not justify changing the source graphs or prompts.

entries.description:
Four bullets, in order:
• A dot plot uses a number line showing all numbers in the range.
• Each dot represents a frequency.
• Dots line up evenly above the line.
• Dot plots reveal clusters, outliers, and gaps.

Annotated dot plot. Horizontal number line has evenly spaced labelled ticks 0 through 10 inclusive, no arrowheads, and centred axis title “Number of days”. Turquoise dots stack vertically: 1:1, 7:1, 8:2, 9:3, 10:2; all other ticks have no dots. A pink rounded label above 1 reads “outlier: very different / to other values”, with a downward pink arrow towards its dot. A pink rounded label above the middle reads “gap: where there is / no data for values”, connected to a horizontal bracket spanning ticks 2–6 with downward end strokes. A pale pink rounded rectangular region surrounds the dots at 7–10. A pink rounded label to its right reads “cluster: data collected / close to one value”, with a left-pointing arrow towards the region.

findings.description: Independent source inventory only. No fidelity, layout or editorial acceptance is claimed. No candidates or repository code were inspected.

Attached page 32 was inspected as teaching context. It establishes that divided bars and sector graphs show parts of a whole and demonstrates proportional scaling of percentages and monetary amounts. Page 36 supplies the directly applicable segment-length method through its Art and Photography calculations. Page 37 is subsequent context and is not needed for these calculations; its image was not inspected.

Visible answer annotations and completed graphs are inventoried separately from student givens. Their classification follows the prompts, response spaces and completed content, rather than colour alone. The black Art calculation is a student-visible worked demonstration.

The instruction refers to calculations for the first two subjects as shown, but Photography still contains a dotted result blank. Preserve both the instruction and that additional completion requirement pending editorial review.

The completed blue bar overlays the original scaffold. Only part of the underlying black outline is independently visible. Its complete original topology and height cannot be established from this image. The required final printed length is explicitly 120 mm.

Part d supplies a new table without explicitly asking for its missing Renewables value. The response requirement is inferred from the empty student cell and supplied 8% answer; retain this ambiguity for review.

Both supplied graph solutions use Gas in place of Natural Gas and appear to use Renwble for Renewables. The narrow renewable labels cross segment boundaries. Preserve these source features in evidence; review wording and final-size label placement together before reconstruction.

The 2020 supplied graph lacks a visible left closing edge. The question does not ask students to diagnose a defective graph, so intentionality is unresolved. Do not silently treat the source as a closed rectangle.
The dataset is described as energy sources or energy mix, but part g refers to electricity generated. These quantities are not automatically equivalent. The source supplies no clarification.

The supplied answer speculates that total electricity increased substantially. No totals are given. The supported conclusion is that doubling the proportion alone does not establish doubling the amount.

Independent calculations confirm the total of 120, all five elective-bar lengths, the missing 4% and 8%, and the proportional graph divisions. Calculations use the supplied values as the exercise data; the historical energy figures were not independently verified.

No cover, syllabus code, syllabus statement, triangle, sector diagram, attribution label or additional independent exercise is present on target page 36. Context-page content is not duplicated into the target inventory.

findings.description: The whole of target page 42 and supplemental page 43 were inspected. Page 42 contains teaching prose and supplied graphical demonstrations, with no independent exercise questions, numbered parts, response blanks, syllabus statements or cover wording. The five table frequencies agree visually with all three histogram occurrences and the five nonzero polygon vertices. Their independently calculated total is 57 + 29 + 31 + 61 + 26 = 204 observations. This total is a verification result, not printed source content.

“Connect the column centres” is imprecise prose: the supplied polygon joins the centres of the top edges, not the geometric centres of the rectangular columns. Preserve the original wording and record any clarification as an editorial decision.
